region.text: the Jhalawar districts severed from Kota in 1838 (area 6,977.5 km2 in 1881)

ledger.note: 1838: Jhalawar is dismembered from Kota. "it was resolved in the year 1838, with the grudging consent of the chief of Kota, to dismember the state"; "The districts thus severed from Kota represented one-third (£120,000) of the income of Kota"; "Madan Singh, grandson of Zalim Singh was made the chief" (table: 8 April 1838). The page names no parganas and no area for the transfer of 1838; the 1881 area of Jhalawar (6,977.5 km2) is used for the circle.

region.text: the Jhalawar districts returned to Kota in 1897-1899

ledger.note: 1897-1899: most of Jhalawar goes back to Kota. After Zalim Singh II was deposed in 1896, "the British resolved in 1897 to break up the state, restoring the greater part to Kota, but forming the two districts of Shahabad and the Chaumahla into a new state of area 810 square miles (2,100 km2), which came into existence in 1899". The year is 1899 (the new state's year); the parganas are not named, and the remnant circle is my reading.

sources.title: Kota State
sources.note: Established 1631 (partitioned from Bundi for Rao Madho Singh); British suzerainty from 1817; area 14,828 km2 (1931); merged with the Union of India on 18 April 1948.

sources.title: Bundi State
sources.note: Rao Deva took Bundi in 1241; subsidiary alliance 10 February 1818; area 5,750 km2; silent on the separation of Kota in 1631.

sources.title: Jhalawar State
sources.note: Created 1838 by dismembering Kota (one-third of Kota's income); Madan Singh; Zalim Singh II deposed 1896; the state broken up 1897-1899 and most returned to Kota; area 6,977.5 km2 (1881), 2,106 km2 (1901).

notes: Three pages opened (Kota State, Bundi State, Jhalawar State). Conflicts: the Kota State infobox lists Hriday Narayan Singh (1607-1624) before the first independent ruler Madho Singh (1631), a prior period that is not an independent state on the page; the Jhalawar page has Kota's regent Zalim Singh from 1771 (regency of the infant Umaid Singh I). The page gives no territorial change for Kota from the Mughals or Marathas, none for Shahabad, Chhabra or Pirawa, and no 1949 merger into Rajasthan. british-empire (sa-06) should record the vassal_start for kota-state from 1817 ("British suzerainty, which began in 1817"; 17-gun salute state) to 1947. The Hada states of Bundi and Jhalawar have dossiers in this batch. The remnant of Jhalawar after 1899 and the exact parganas returned to Kota are not on the pages. Gazetteer lacks Kota, Bundi, Jhalawar as places; coordinates are used. Counterpart for the 1948 end: the Rajasthan Union of 1948 (not named on the page) needs a dossier from the post-1947 group.
